title: Trajectory Forcing: Exploiting Diffusion Trajectories for Autoregressive Long Video Generation
claim: Standard sequential models condition on whole histories of atomic tokens, but diffusion chunks hide denoising trajectories that should also be used as context.
layout: 2 stacked panels, left-to-right, curved arc from history bracket to prediction
description: Two stacked rounded panels compare standard autoregressive modeling with autoregressive diffusion. Panel (a), 'Standard AR', shows three dark-outlined boxes labelled '1', '2' and '3' under a large 'Trajectory' brace. A curved arrow runs from the brace to an orange box labelled '4' under the orange word 'Prediction'. Panel (b), 'AR Diffusion', has the same layout, but each token is replaced by a noise-to-clean pair. A dotted noise tile and an arrow lead to a clapperboard video icon with a numbered badge 1, 2 or 3. The fourth pair is orange and marks the chunk being predicted. The 'Trajectory' brace spans all the preceding noise-to-clean steps and arcs to the orange chunk. Navy and orange carry the contrast. The eye goes first to the two brace-and-arc structures.
caption: Standard AR vs.\ AR diffusion. (a) In standard AR (Eq. [ref]), each token is atomic and requires no further generation. The next token is naturally conditioned on all preceding tokens. (b) In AR diffusion, each chunk is generated through $T$ denoising steps that form a trajectory. Following Eq. [ref], each denoising step should be conditioned on the full trajectories of all preceding chunks.
abstract: Autoregressive (AR) modeling is arguably the only way to extend a fixed-length video diffusion model to longer or even streaming videos. However, existing AR diffusion methods use only the previously predicted chunk as context for the next, discarding the intermediate predictions that constitute the chunk's generation history. In contrast, conventional AR models such as LLMs condition on the entire history of preceding tokens. To this end, we propose Trajectory Forcing (TraF), an AR diffusion method that exploits the denoising trajectories of previous video chunks as context. TraF operates under two training regimes: (1) with ground-truth videos, where pseudo-trajectories are constructed from Gaussian interpolations and re-predicted by the model, and (2) with a teacher model, where real trajectories are obtained from the student's own denoising rollout. The first regime naturally provides a strong initialization for the second. On the 5-second VBench benchmark, TraF achieves a Total score of 85.15, outperforming Self Forcing (+0.84) and Causal Forcing (+1.11), with Quality and Semantic improving simultaneously. On 30-second generation---6$\times$ the training horizon---TraF achieves the highest overall quality among all compared methods.
